decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elevated approach to the cup, pitching toward a rim grasp while maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Advance above the cup and progressively point the right gripper downward; keep left arm stationary.
Align open fingers around the right-hand cup rim from above, slowing before contact.
Lower fingertips just inside/outside the cup rim and close gently to a full holding target; retention remains to be checked visually.
Test cup retention by lifting with right gripper closed; start an elevated left-arm approach to the vase rim.
Cup remains visibly retained. Advance left arm above the vase for a rim pinch, keeping both arms separated.
Orient the left fingers downward over the vase's left rim; right arm holds the cup steady.
Reduce opening to clear vase shoulders, settle a few millimeters onto the left lip, and close for a rim grasp. Contact location is uncertain.
Lift the vase slightly to check retention, and bring the retained cup inward while preserving both grasp orientations.
Vase stayed on the table after the lift test. Reopen and descend deeper around its left lip before attempting another pinch.
Fingers now straddle the vase lip. Close at the observed contact height and make a short lift to check retention.
The vase has not followed the lift. Reattempt a deeper lip pinch with a narrower opening to avoid the vase shoulder.
Hold the deeper rim pinch closed and make a slow lift test before moving the vase laterally.
Rim pinches have not retained the vase. Withdraw and turn the left gripper toward a horizontal neck grasp instead.
Lower the open left gripper to surround the vase neck from the front, keeping the cup steady in the right hand.
Close around the vase neck and test a small vertical lift; retain the cup without further tilt.
Continue a short, slow vase lift and slight inward motion to verify whether the side grasp carries it.
The vase did not follow. Recenter left fingers and reach farther around its neck rather than closing in front of it.
Lower around the neck below the lip while keeping the deeper forward reach; begin closing only after height alignment.
Close at the observed neck contact rather than pushing farther downward, then test a small lift.
Test the neck grasp with a slow upward and inward motion; judge vase retention from its movement in the head view.
The vase again stayed behind. Reposition with level fingers for a deeper, lower side grasp below its flared lip.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller descent and rotation increments, leveling the fingers above the vase neck.
Descend level, open fingers below the vase lip to enclose the neck, with a small forward adjustment.
Close the level left fingers around the neck at the current contact height, then test retention with a short lift.
The previous pinch slipped over the flared lip. Lower the level jaws below the rim to grasp the narrower neck instead.
Test gentle inward translation at the current vase contact, keeping it supported by the table rather than lifting over the flared lip.
Vase does not move with contact; switch to a cup handoff so the left arm can pour in its own workspace. Withdraw left and begin presenting the held cup inward.
Bring the left gripper up and inward for a body handoff. Present the cup at a moderate tilt while keeping its balls retained.
Continue the left-arm handoff approach with open jaws, orienting across the cup body while the right arm holds still.
Bring the left fingers closer around the cup body for a handoff, with the left wrist remaining on its own side and the right grasp closed.
Settle the left fingers around the cup body and close fully while the right hand continues supporting its rim.
Release the right rim pinch and withdraw its fingers along their approach direction while the left body grasp stays fully closed.
Cup is retained by the left hand. Carry it leftward and begin restoring upright orientation while the empty right arm withdraws toward home.
Carry the cup upright toward the vase in the left workspace; continue the empty right arm's gradual return.
Replan with smaller leftward increments after the IK interruption, keeping a slight cup pitch to avoid the wrist singularity and approach the vase.
Use smaller steps and turn the left wrist toward a less singular yaw while keeping the cup upright; continue the empty right arm's return.
Position the cup on the left side of the vase opening and introduce a modest pouring tilt, keeping the balls below the rim until alignment is checked.
No motion executed in the rejected chunk. Halve the cup approach and tilt increments to preserve wrist-joint continuity.
Bring the cup lip closer above the vase while gradually increasing its rightward pouring tilt; keep the right arm parked.
Increase the pouring tilt while compensating wrist translation to keep the cup's lower lip above the vase opening.
Tilt farther toward the vase, translating inward to keep the pouring edge over its mouth as the cup rotates.
Advance the cup's pouring edge toward the vase center while tipping slightly past horizontal; watch for ball transfer.
Balls are visibly leaving the cup toward the vase. Hold the pouring pose steady to let the remaining balls settle.
The cup is empty, but several balls appear outside the vase. Begin restoring the cup upright and clearing the opening for a recovery attempt.
Continue returning the empty cup upright and move it away from the vase before setting it down.
Move the empty cup toward a clear area in front of the vase and continue restoring it upright, retaining the grasp.
Finish uprighting the empty cup while lowering it toward a clear tabletop placement in the left workspace.
Replan with small increments after the IK interruption, lowering the upright cup while keeping elbow configuration continuous.
Lower the upright empty cup toward tabletop support before opening the left gripper.
Set the upright empty cup down, open the left fingers, and begin a short withdrawal without disturbing the nearby vase or balls.
Leave the cup upright and withdraw the left hand upward, orienting for a careful attempt to recover a spilled ball.
The previous chunk executed no motion. Halve withdrawal and orientation increments to maintain joint continuity while clearing the cup.
Move above the spilled ball to the right of the cup, progressively orienting the left fingers downward and keeping clearance over the upright cup.
Clear the cup and align a downward pinch above the spilled ball on its right; leave the right arm at home.
Align the narrow downward jaws with the loose ball beside the cup, descending cautiously for an individual recovery grasp.
Lower the centered fingers to the ball, close fully, and begin a small retention test lift.
Lift the pinched ball vertically with the left gripper closed and check whether it stays between the fingers.
The ball did not stay in the pinch. Reopen narrowly and descend slightly deeper to grasp its sides near table height.
Finish closing with the ball centered between the jaws, then make a slow, short lift to test retention.
The ball remained on the table. Recenter slightly left and place the fingers lower around its sides before closing.
Allow the centered ball pinch to finish closing at the observed contact pose, then lift slowly to verify retention.
Lift the closed pinch clear of the table and toward the vase to inspect whether the ball followed; retention remains uncertain.
The ball stayed on the table. Reapproach with the fingertips shifted toward the robot to correct the fore-aft alignment, using a narrow opening.
